summary: Superconducting niobium nitride (NbN) thin films were deposited by plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD) using the metal organic precursor (tert-butylimido)-tris (diethylamino)-niobium (TBTDEN) and hydrogen plasma. The study aimed to optimize the deposition process to achieve low resistivity and high superconducting transition temperature (TC). The process was optimized to reduce oxygen concentration in the films, which significantly affected the resistivity and TC. The best results were achieved at a deposition temperature of 400°C and a plasma pressure of 6 mTorr, resulting in a TC of 10.2 K and a resistivity of 2.5 µΩ·cm.
